## Design Health Score

| # | Heuristic | Score | Key issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visibility of system status | 3 | Dirty-state + beforeunload on Controls Settings; toasts everywhere. Settings tab row above the h1 with no page context. |
| 2 | Match system / real world | 3 | "Jurisdiction" for Tax; "SMB mode" pill explained only by tooltip; warn-check reference cites `lib/gates/`. |
| 3 | User control and freedom | 3 | Confirm dialogs on destructive member actions, Touchless preview. No Discard on the long Controls form; no undo after Remove member. |
| 4 | Consistency and standards | 1 | Two design systems (shadcn Card vs Panel/hairlines), two "Settings" labels, two "Rules" (settings/rules vs automation/vendors), two tab grammars, duplicate gear icons. |
| 5 | Error prevention | 3 | Last-owner/last-reviewer guards, band validation, dry-run warn checks. `settings/budgets` registered (lib/modules/index.ts:90) with no page → 404. |
| 6 | Recognition rather than recall | 2 | Approvals empty state sends you to "Settings → Modules" in the other tree; Warn checks reachable only by URL. |
| 7 | Flexibility and efficiency | 1 | No shortcuts, no bulk member actions, no search on Members/Vendors/Rules, switcher is an unfiltered scroll. |
| 8 | Aesthetic and minimalist | 2 | Workspace page = seven equal cards; 8–11 flat tabs wrap to 2 lines at 1440, 3 at 390 (confirmed by screenshot). |
| 9 | Error recovery | 3 | Field-adjacent errors; some raw server strings reach toasts. |
| 10 | Help and documentation | 2 | Good panel notes; inline toggle explanation hidden in `title`; only reference block is for developers. |
| **Total** | | **23/40** | **Acceptable** |

## Design specificity verdict

Split. Controls is authored for DocuBite (controls-spine.tsx, autonomy ladder, Touchless impact estimate). Settings is category-interchangeable shadcn (text-3xl h1, stacked Cards, text-muted-foreground). The two areas don't share a visual language; every click between them crosses a product seam.

Deterministic scan: static `impeccable detect` → 2 findings (gray-on-color, `text-slate-500 on bg-red-50`, category-account-mapping-table.tsx:76, category-nature-table.tsx:100).

In-page detector (live dev server, 1440 / 390):

| Surface | 1440 | 390 | Page-specific (beyond 5 shell-level findings) |
|---|---|---|---|
| settings/workspace | 10 | 9 | nested-cards ×3; low-contrast 4.3:1 on "Owner" pill |
| settings/modules | 11 | 8 | low-contrast 4.3:1 on "On" pills ×3; line-length ×2 |
| settings/rules | 7 | 5 | line-length |
| automation (Controls) | 6 | 5 | — |
| automation/settings | 10 | 5 | line-length ×4 (87–150 ch) |
| automation/approvals | 11 | 9 | tiny-text 11px ×2; text-occlusion ×2 in stage details |

Shell-level findings shared by every page: ai-color-palette on the switcher avatar ×2, text-overflow on the switcher name (1440), overused-font Inter, layout-transition height on body, dark-glow on body — the shell's, not this ticket's. No page errors.

## Priority issues

- [P1] Two admin trees, two "Settings", two "Rules". Fix: one Admin tree. Command: organize → impeccable shape.
- [P1] Settings and Controls render as two products (Card+text-3xl vs Panel+font-display 26px+#e6ebf1; 128px column jump). Fix: Panel/Ledger as the admin primitive; hex hairlines to tokens. Command: impeccable extract, layout.
- [P1] 8–11 flat settings tabs, duplicate icons, dead settings/budgets link. Fix: ≤4 groups; add landmark icon; ship or drop budgets. Command: organize, impeccable distill.
- [P2] /settings/workspace is seven unrelated cards with no primary. Command: impeccable distill, layout.
- [P2] Warn checks is an orphaned owner-only page with developer copy. Command: articulate, impeccable clarify.

## What's working

1. controls-spine.tsx — annotated pipeline with jointAria.
2. automation-config-form.tsx Touchless confirm with 30-day impact estimate.
3. setting-toggle.tsx — mandatory one-sentence explanation on every admin toggle (#208).

## Persona red flags

Alex: no keyboard path; one-row members; no search on Vendors; single bottom Save. Sam: settings-nav has no aria-label; mode pill title-only; inline toggle explanation needs hover; spine counts read "Review 14"; line-through as disabled. Priya (six client companies): unfiltered switcher with identical initial tiles; every setting configured six times; account-level Security inside each workspace; no cross-workspace membership view; firm mode derived per workspace.

## Minor observations

Templates tab still first-class though Worksheets are unplugged (#238) and Modules lists Worksheets "On"; three avatar treatments; settings/email toLocaleString server-side; "Health Checks" the only two-word bottom item; padEnd alignment in warn-check list.

## Questions to consider

1. Is Controls actually Admin wearing a work-surface costume?
2. Should the Admin landing be a spine rather than a tab strip?
3. Should Admin be sectioned by scope (You · This company · This organisation)?
4. Should "is this a firm-managed client?" be asked once rather than derived?
5. Why doesn't every consequential admin change get the Touchless 30-day-impact treatment?

content.text:
Facts in hand: Templates = `DocumentTemplate` extraction templates grouped by *file* (files/worksheets are unplugged, so the page is orphaned); Reports = dictation report templates (dictation unplugged; the page already `notFound()`s); custom fields live on `DocumentTemplate`; the account menu carries only sign-out.

## Context (Intent — established once)

- **Users of Admin:** (1) the workspace **owner** — a finance lead who configures once, then returns monthly to add a person, change who approves, or raise autonomy; (2) **Priya**, an accountant running several client companies, who wants one login, one users list, and to stop configuring the same thing six times (PRODUCT.md secondary user; research #230 found the grouping missing). Both act under low frequency / high consequence: a wrong toggle silently changes what publishes.
- **Product:** existing Next.js app; Admin today is split across Settings (10 tabs) and Controls (5 tabs) — critique 23/40.
- **Constraints:** isolation is per-workspace (scope guard + RLS keyed on `workspace_id`); 71/80 models carry `workspaceId`; removals need owner sign-off (#237); mobile is Approval-only (#189).
- **Ethical stance:** every consequential setting states its consequence (the #208 contract); no toggle defaults to more automation than the owner chose; org membership must never silently become entity access.
- **Success:** an owner adds a user to two companies with different roles in one flow; the settings tab wall (8–11) becomes ≤4 groups; Admin critiques ≥28/40 with zero page-specific detector findings.
- **Assumption named:** no user research on multi-company accountants exists; Priya is inferred from PRODUCT.md and should be validated (`investigate` is not blocking this shape).

**Impeccable mode:** Operate. Incumbent inspected above.

## Round 1 — the model (Intent: `blueprint` / `organize`; domain-modeling)

❓ **Q1** - **Company = Workspace, or Company below Workspace?** Research #230 laid out Option A (Workspace *is* the Company; add `Organization` above, nullable `Workspace.organizationId`, `OrganizationMember`) versus Option B (re-key 71 models under a new Company).

➡️ **Option A.** Evidence: 71/80 models keyed on `workspaceId`, one Bigcapital org per workspace (ADR-001), jurisdiction/currency/fiscal year already per workspace, both isolation layers keyed on `workspace_id`, and the schema's own note that "multi-entity graduates to a future decision". Additive and reversible; B is neither. This is an ADR (hard to reverse, surprising later, real trade-off).

---

❓ **Q2** - **Does Organization membership ever imply entity access?**

➡️ **No.** `WorkspaceMember` stays the only grant; the scope guard and RLS remain sufficient unchanged. Vic's own model adds each entity to a user explicitly with its own ✕ (tour §Admin → Users). Principle: ethical defaults / least privilege — a firm-wide grant would be a silent cross-tenant widening.

---

❓ **Q3** - **Role axes: one or two?** Vic has User Type (Accountant/Approver) *and* User Level per entity. DocuBite has `owner | reviewer | member` per workspace.

➡️ **Two axes, both minimal.** Organization role: `admin | member` on `OrganizationMember` (admin manages Companies, Users, invitations across the org). Entity role: the existing `owner | reviewer | member` on `WorkspaceMember`, unchanged. Do **not** import Accountant/Approver: Approver is already a *fact* of `ApprovalWorkflowStage` assignment (glossary), not a role, and reviewer + owner already cover Vic's User Levels. Principle: don't add vocabulary the glossary already covers (#233's one-vocabulary rule).

---

❓ **Q4** - **What happens to the `personal` workspace** for a user who belongs to an organization?

➡️ **It stays, ungrouped, labelled "Personal"** at the bottom of the switcher, and never appears in Organization › Companies. Not retired (that is a removal) and not made the default company (it has no ledger role). Smallest reversible option.

---

❓ **Q5** - **Cross-company queries and isolation.** Organization › Dashboard and Users are multi-workspace queries by definition.

➡️ **Rule: `unscoped()` + explicit `workspaceId: { in: memberWorkspaceIds }`, where the ids come from `WorkspaceMember` — never from `OrganizationMember`.** RLS stays per-workspace (no org-aware policy; it is not live anyway). **Closing the 32-model guard-set gap is a prerequisite task** before the first cross-company screen ships, because a switcher makes cross-workspace navigation routine (research §Isolation). This is an AFK task ticket.

---

❓ **Q6** - **Invitations across companies.**

➡️ **An org admin invites one email into N companies in one action, choosing a role per company;** acceptance upserts N `WorkspaceMember` rows plus one `OrganizationMember(member)`. Per-workspace invite by an owner stays as-is. Principle: the success criterion in Context; Vic's Companies tab per user is the read side of this.

---

❓ **Q7** - **Platform `User.role = "admin"` vs organization admin.**

➡️ **Unrelated axes, stays that way.** Platform admin unlocks `/admin-next` only (`lib/admin.ts`); it never grants org or entity access. Guard against the accident the research warns of.

---

❓ **Q8** - **What is the user-facing word: Workspace or Company?**

➡️ **"Company" in Admin, the switcher and every org-level surface; "Workspace" stays the storage and URL term.** Vic wins ties, and PRODUCT.md's users say "client company", not "workspace". Glossary gains **Company** and **Organization**; "Workspace" keeps its technical meaning. Personal workspaces are shown as "Personal", never "Company".

**Answers taken: Q1–Q8 as recommended.** (Rule: map Notes → research evidence → Intent ethical defaults.)

## Round 2 — the IA and each section (Intent: `organize` / `journey` / `fortify`)

❓ **Q9** - **Is Admin one destination that replaces Settings and Controls?** Today: rail bottom "Settings" (10 tabs) and rail primary "Controls" (5 tabs).

➡️ **Yes. One rail item, "Admin", at the bottom of the rail where Settings sits; Controls leaves the primary spine and its contents move into Admin.** Critique P1 #1 (two trees, two "Settings", two "Rules") is only resolvable this way, and the map's Notes say Controls' rail fate waits on this ticket. Nothing is removed — the pages relocate. The rail's primary spine becomes: Invoices · POs │ Receipts · Bank Statements │ Exceptions · Payments (#251) · Finance · Archive; secondary: Close · Health Checks; bottom: Activity · Admin.

---

❓ **Q10** - **Admin's own navigation: Vic's two groups, mapped onto DocuBite.** Vic: ORGANIZATION (Dashboard, Companies, Users) · COMPANY (Configuration, Approval Flows, PO Mismatch Flows). DocuBite has 15 destinations to home.

➡️ Adopt Vic's two groups and map every incumbent page into them:

| Group | Section | Absorbs |
|---|---|---|
| ORGANIZATION | Dashboard | new (Q16) |
| | Companies | new; "Create a team workspace" card |
| | Users | Members table + Invitations + per-company roles |
| COMPANY | Configuration | field table (Q11) · autonomy ladder, blocks, policy, amount bands (Controls › Settings) · warn checks · AI extraction toggle · email intake · jurisdiction · modules ("What's on") |
| | Approval Flows | Controls › Approval workflows + default flow (Q12) |
| | PO Mismatch Flows | Controls › Matches + PO quantity tolerance + match-variance approver (Q13) |
| | Suppliers | `settings/rules` + Controls › Vendors merged — one "Supplier rules" |
| | Integrations | Integrations + Account mapping (shown only when integrations are enabled) |

**Account-level items leave Admin:** Security (MFA, sessions) and "Reset the tour" move to the **account menu** (`account-menu.tsx`), which today only signs out. **Suppliers** and **Integrations** are DocuBite additions to Vic's COMPANY group — documented exceptions, because Vic has no supplier rules or connector settings on the tour. Danger zone stays at the bottom of Companies › (this company).

---

❓ **Q11** - **Does the Configuration field table drive queue columns (metadata-driven) or only the Detail pane?**

➡️ **Both, with a boundary.** Per document type, the table lists `lib/doc-types.ts` canonical keys plus that type's `DocumentTemplate` custom fields, with **Editable · Required · Width** and ✕ on custom fields only. *Editable* and *Required* drive the Detail pane (Required also feeds the "Block approval if a required field is missing" toggle). *Width* and row order drive each queue's **system views' default columns**; a user's saved view still overrides visible columns (glossary: Saved view). Vic's Width column is meaningless unless it reaches the list, so "Vic wins ties" settles it; the boundary keeps #225's per-queue `QueueColumn` arrays as the source of *what a column can be* — Configuration chooses among them, it does not invent columns. Fog item "Metadata-driven columns" graduates into the Configuration execution ticket.

---

❓ **Q12** - **Approval Flows.** #227 handed this ticket the **workspace default approval flow** (auto-starts an Approval when an invoice reaches In review with no blocking check).

➡️ **Approval Flows = today's list + editor, plus one "Default flow" selector at the top with the consequence sentence:** "Starts on its own when an invoice reaches In review with no blocking check. Until one is chosen, approvals start by hand from the Invoices bulk bar." Off by default (ethical default: no automation the owner didn't choose). The flow editor keeps stages, named approvers, amount thresholds.

---

❓ **Q13** - **PO Mismatch Flows.** #227 decision 4: the flow names the approver for a blocked `match-variance` gate; until then the current stage's approver decides. #228 chose the match-variance percent and derived Fully invoiced.

➡️ **One page with two panels: Tolerances** (PO quantity tolerance %, match-variance %, each with its consequence sentence and the "= only while View PO is on" rule from #228) **and Who approves a mismatch** — a named-approver list with the default "the current stage's approver" shown as the in-force value. Controls › Matches' match history moves here as its read-only log. Vic's name "PO Mismatch Flows" is kept.

---

❓ **Q14** - **Users.**

➡️ **Org-level list on the #225 Queue-screen shell** (list + right Detail pane; Vic: Users list + right panel with Information / Companies tabs). Row: name · email · org role · number of companies. Pane tabs: **Information** (name, email, org role) · **Companies** (one expandable section per company with its entity role select and ✕ remove; "Add to a company" at the bottom). Personal workspaces never listed. Last-owner / last-reviewer guards from `members-table.tsx` carry over per company. For a user with no organization, Users shows only this company's members — same screen, one company.

---

❓ **Q15** - **Companies.**

➡️ **List of the organization's companies** (name · country · currency · jurisdiction · members · your role) on the same shell; pane shows the company's summary and an **Open** action that switches to it. **"Add a company"** creates a team workspace inside the organization (replaces the "Create a team workspace" card). **Organization creation:** the first time an owner of a team workspace opens Admin › Companies, one form: "Name your organization" — creating it groups that workspace; other team workspaces the same user owns get a "Move into ‹org›" action. No auto-grouping (autonomy: the user says which workspaces belong together).

---

❓ **Q16** - **Organization › Dashboard** — Vic's per-entity rollups (open invoices / pending approvals / pending PO mismatch approvals per company). #237 removed the workspace Dashboard and put reporting out of scope.

➡️ **Adopt Vic's rollups, and only them: three plain tables, entity name → count → link, no charts.** This is triage across companies (the "multi-workspace day" fog item), not reporting; #237's removal was of the *workspace* home overview. **Shown only when the organization has ≥2 companies;** with one company the Dashboard entry is absent and Admin lands on Configuration. Counts are the same Ready-to-Approve / open-Exception counts the rail badges use, per company. Name: **Dashboard**, as Vic — CONTEXT.md's avoid list is about the *workspace home*, which this is not; the glossary entry will say so.

---

❓ **Q17** - **The rail, the switcher and `/workspaces` with many companies.**

➡️ **Switcher:** grouped by organization with the company's role rendered per entry (the `role` prop is passed and unused today), Personal last, a filter input once there are more than 6 entries. **`/workspaces`:** stays a forwarder when the user has one membership; with more than one it becomes the Companies picker (same list as Admin › Companies, read-only). The rail keeps its position as the collapsible icon rail (#224 Q5, a documented exception to Vic's top bar).

---

❓ **Q18** - **Phone.** #189: mobile is Approval-only; #113's compact-navigation bullet was superseded for Approval. Today the 4th tab is "Settings" and opens a three-line tab wall.

➡️ **Admin is desktop-only; the phone's 4th slot becomes "Account"** (profile, security, switch company, sign out — the account menu re-composed). Admin pages keep rendering content-only on a phone if deep-linked (nothing is removed) but are not in the tab bar and show a one-line "Admin is a desktop area" note above the content. This waits on #232 for the phone home's shape; #232 gains a note.

---

❓ **Q19** - **State inventory** (`fortify`) for Admin as a whole.

➡️ Every execution ticket ships these states, none optional: *no organization yet* (Companies shows the naming form; Dashboard absent; Users = this company); *one company* (no Dashboard); *many companies* (grouped switcher, filter at >6); *member, not owner* (Configuration read-only with "Ask an owner" in place of Save — today's `notFound()` on Controls › Settings is a dead end, critique H6); *last owner / last reviewer* (guards); *integrations off* (Integrations section absent, not disabled); *unsaved changes on navigate* (dirty marker + `beforeunload`, from Controls today); *save failed* (field-adjacent error, form preserved); *company removed while open in another tab* (the #238 workspace not-found boundary).

**Answers taken: Q9–Q19 as recommended.** (Rules: Vic wins ties for Q9, Q10, Q13, Q14, Q16; documented exceptions kept for Q17; #227/#228 decisions for Q12–Q13; ethical defaults for Q12; #189 for Q18.)

## Round 3 — rendering (Impeccable: `shape`, then `layout` / `distill` / `clarify` / `adapt`)

❓ **Q20** - **Admin's shell: Vic's left two-group nav or the incumbent top tab strip?**

# An invoice's paid state is derived, ledger first, then DocuBite's own payment records

DocuBite prepares payment files and never moves money, so "paid" was only ever a fact the ledger sync reported (`models/ledger-payments.ts`); a workspace without a connected ledger could never mark anything paid, and a downloaded payment file left no trace on the invoice (#229, map #226). We decided that Mark as paid and a paid payment batch write **payment records** (an amount, a date, a method, an optional reference) on DocuBite's side, and that the invoice's paid state is **derived** at read time: the ledger's confirmation wins when it exists; otherwise the sum of payment records against the amount due decides Paid, Partially paid or Unpaid, and membership of a pending or approved batch reads as Scheduled. Payment records are never pushed to the ledger by this path — ledger placement stays the Finance push's job — so a record and a ledger line can disagree, and the row must say which source it is reading.

## Considered options

- **Store `paidAt` on the Document.** Rejected: no partial payments, no reversal trail, and it would silently overwrite the ledger's answer.
- **Only trust the ledger.** Rejected: most workspaces in the sandbox have no ledger connected, and a batch that was uploaded to the bank would still read Unpaid the following week ("did I already pay this?" had no answer, Finance critique 14/40).
- **Push a payment to the ledger on Mark as paid.** Rejected for this map: approval never publishes (#227) and the ledger hand-off is #248's decision.

## Consequences

- `BillRow.paymentStatus` grows a `source: "ledger" | "recorded"` alongside the derived state, and the queue pill says "Paid (recorded)" when the ledger has not confirmed.
- Removing a payment record needs a reason and an audit event; nothing else can flip Paid back to Unpaid.
- The ledger sync overriding a recorded payment is a counter-metric worth watching (measure, #229 Q17).

# The Workspace is the Company; an Organization groups Workspaces above it, and never grants access to them

DocuBite needs Vic.ai's "one login, many companies" Admin (Companies, an organization-wide Users list, per-entity roles) on map #226 (#231). The research on #230 found that a Workspace already carries everything an entity needs — country, currency, timezone, fiscal year, tax jurisdiction, VAT scheme, matching tolerance, HIPAA posture, its own suppliers and one Bigcapital ledger organization (ADR-001) — that 71 of 80 models are keyed on `workspaceId`, and that both isolation layers (the Prisma scope guard and Postgres RLS) key on `workspace_id`. We decided that **the Workspace is the Company** (shown as "Company" in Admin and the switcher, "Personal" for the auto-created one), that an additive **Organization** (`Workspace.organizationId` nullable, plus an `OrganizationMember` join carrying `admin | member`) groups companies for the accountant running several clients, and that **organization membership never implies entity access**: `WorkspaceMember` stays the only grant, and every organization-wide query is written as `unscoped()` with an explicit `workspaceId IN (…)` list derived from `WorkspaceMember` rows, never from `OrganizationMember`.

## Considered options

- **Company below Workspace (Workspace becomes the firm).** Rejected: every entity-level field and 71 `workspaceId` columns would have to move to a new `Company`, both isolation layers re-keyed, and `BigcapitalAccount.workspaceId @unique` (one ledger per entity) would break.
- **Organization membership grants access to all its companies.** Rejected: it would make firm membership a silent cross-tenant widening and make the per-workspace scope guard and RLS insufficient; Vic's own model adds each entity to a user explicitly.
- **No grouping — keep the flat switcher.** Rejected: the accountant configures the same thing per client and has no cross-company users list; that is the gap the research found.

## Consequences

- `WorkspaceMember.role` (`owner | reviewer | member`) stays the per-entity role; `OrganizationMember.role` is `admin | member` and only governs Companies, Users and invitations in Admin. Platform `User.role = "admin"` remains a third, unrelated axis (`lib/admin.ts`).
- Closing the scope-guard gap (32 `workspaceId` models outside `WORKSPACE_SCOPED_MODELS`) is a prerequisite for the first cross-company screen, because a company switcher makes cross-workspace navigation by one user routine.
- Personal workspaces are never members of an organization and never appear in Companies.
- An invitation can name several companies with a role in each; acceptance writes one `WorkspaceMember` row per company.

# TaxHacker Product Context

This glossary defines the product language used for the authenticated workspace experience and its document-to-ledger workflow.

## Authenticated workspace experience

**Workspace home**:
The Invoices queue. Opening a workspace lands the user on their work, not on a summary of it; "what needs me" is read from the rail badges and the queue's own counts. There is no separate overview surface.
_Avoid_: Dashboard, landing page, overview, next best action

**Unplugged surface**:
A feature the product no longer shows or routes to, kept only so it can be brought back deliberately. Worksheets, Expenses and Dictation are unplugged. An unplugged surface has no navigation entry, no row or bulk action, no badge, and its addresses do not open.
_Avoid_: Hidden, deprecated, legacy

**Core workflow destinations**:
Invoices, Purchase Orders, Receipts, Bank Statements, Exceptions, Finance, and Archive: the permission-filtered peer surfaces representing typed intake, escalated work, booked outcome, and the permanent source record. The four typed intake destinations replace the former single "Documents" surface.

**Document**:
The storage-and-extraction primitive underlying every typed destination. Every Invoice, Purchase Order, Receipt, and Bank Statement is a Document, but "Document" is no longer itself a user-facing destination — the user asserts which typed destination a Document belongs to at upload time, and that assertion is authoritative.
_Avoid_: Using "Document" as a destination name; unclassified/pending-classification states

**Invoice**:
The typed destination for a bill received from a supplier. Absorbs the former Documents/Bills surface; aging is a filter chip and a saved view here, and paying an approved invoice happens on Bill Pay, not on this queue.

**Purchase Order**:
The typed destination for a purchase order, paired with Invoices for matching and cumulative line-item comparison against what has already been invoiced against it.

**Receipt**:
The typed destination for a receipt. Absorbs expense-claim creation and approval as an action on selected rows rather than as its own destination.

**Bank Statement**:
The typed destination for a bank statement. The reviewer asserts the issuing institution; the first statement for that institution becomes its saved layout, and later uploads are checked against it for drift.

**Check**:
A tri-valued (pass/warn/fail), explainable comparison that states in plain language why a value is flagged, anchored to the field, cell, or row it concerns. "Mismatch" names one Check status, not the category.
_Avoid_: Discrepancy, issue, error (as the umbrella term)

**Line match**:
An invoice line's assigned Purchase Order line — guessed by description similarity, or set by hand in Match manually. A line below the similarity threshold has no line match and is not compared.
_Avoid_: Line pairing, line mapping

**Match manually**:
The named in-row mode on an invoice's line items that confirms, replaces or rejects its Purchase Order and reassigns line matches; the checks re-run when it is left. It changes the facts and needs no reason; it is not Override Mode, which accepts a variance with a reason.
_Avoid_: Manual Match Mode (Vic's name), re-match, Override (for a match change)

**Override Mode**:
The screen-scoped mode in which a soft check or gate can be overridden, each override attributed and recorded with a required reason. Hard gates are out of its reach.
_Avoid_: Bypass, force approve

**Fully invoiced**:
A Purchase Order whose every line has been invoiced to at least its ordered quantity. Derived, never set by hand.
_Avoid_: Closed PO, consumed

**Saved view**:
A named, reusable filter/sort/column configuration on a list screen. System views are seeded per screen and are not editable or deletable; a user can duplicate one into an editable, optionally shared, view.

**Work item**:
A single unit of pending work surfaced in a Next-action queue — a document awaiting review or a match awaiting confirmation. An approval awaiting a decision is an Approval, not a work item; it is worked by an Approver, not an assignee.

**Approval**:
A run started on an invoice by a person, moving through the stages of an approval flow until it is approved, rejected, or sent back for review. An invoice nobody has started an approval on is under review, not awaiting approval.
_Avoid_: Review task (the storage record), sign-off (as the umbrella term)

**Approver**:
The person who can decide the current stage of an Approval — a stage's named approver, or any owner where the stage names nobody. Distinct from an assignee, who works a review.
_Avoid_: Reviewer (that is who prepares the row), assignee

**Ready to Approve**:
The personal system view on the Approvals destination: every Approval whose current stage the signed-in person can decide, including rows that are not yet eligible, shown with the reason. The badge on the rail counts this view and nothing else.
_Avoid_: Pending approvals (that is the workspace-wide count), inbox

**Send back for review**:
The reversible middle path on an Approval: the stage is not decided, the invoice returns to review with a required reason, and the run can be restarted. Reject ends the run.
_Avoid_: Reopen, cancel (that withdraws a run before any stage is decided)

**Not eligible**:
An Approval that is visible to its Approver but cannot be decided yet because a hard check failed or an escalation is open on the invoice. Never hidden, never overridable from Approvals; the reason is shown on the row.

**Bill Pay**:
The queue of approved, unpaid invoices from which payment batches are created. An invoice reaches it only once its processing state is Approved; one that cannot be paid yet (no supplier bank details) stays visible with the reason.
_Avoid_: Payables, payment run (the queue), pay list

**Payment batch**:
A named set of approved invoices, one payer account and one currency, submitted by a member for an owner's decision. Pending approval, then Approved (its payment file can be downloaded), then Paid; or Rejected with a reason. Whether the file has been downloaded is a fact shown on the batch, not a state. A batch never moves money.
_Avoid_: Payment run, remittance (that is the advice sent to the supplier), transfer

**Payer account**:
A named workspace bank account a payment batch is to be paid from — a label that tells the uploader which bank portal the file belongs to. DocuBite never holds the account's credentials and the file never carries its number.
_Avoid_: Pay From (Vic's column label is fine on screen; the concept is the payer account), funding source, bank connection

**Payment terms**:
A supplier's net days and, when offered, an early-payment discount: the percent and the days within which it applies, shown as "2/10 net 30". A supplier without a discount shows no discount claim and no discount countdown.
_Avoid_: Terms code, "2-10-30"

**Payment record**:
A DocuBite-side fact that an amount was paid against an invoice on a date, by a batch or by hand (Mark as paid). An invoice's paid state is derived from the ledger when it confirms payment, otherwise from its payment records. A payment record can be removed with a reason.
_Avoid_: Mark as paid (the action, not the record), settlement, ledger payment (that is the ledger's own line)

**Immersive surface**:
A document-detail or worksheet page that temporarily takes over the viewport while preserving workspace identity, a clear return action, and relevant workspace status.

**Queue screen**:
A typed destination's list view (Invoices, Purchase Orders, Receipts, Bank Statements, Exceptions). The queue fills the work area; selecting a row opens the Detail pane beside it, and the operator never leaves the screen to review, approve, or resolve a row.

**Detail pane**:
The single right-hand pane on a Queue screen that shows the selected row's extracted fields beside its source document, with its approval chain, audit trail, and open checks as tabs. There is one Detail pane per Queue screen; it is the only place a row's detail opens in place.

**Origin context**:
The workspace, list, filters, position, and workflow state from which a user opened a detail or action surface. Returning from that surface restores the origin context whenever it still exists.

**Workflow operation**:
An in-progress or recently completed unit of work such as extraction, sync, review assignment, worksheet placement, approval, or publish. An operation remains discoverable after navigation so the user can understand what happened and what to do next.

**Operation status**:
The user-facing progress and outcome for a workflow operation, shown inline where the operation began and in the workspace activity/status area. It includes the current step, progress when known, and a plain-language next action.

**Partial outcome**:
A batch result in which individual items may succeed, need review, be skipped, be canceled, or fail. Partial outcomes remain visible per item rather than being collapsed into one batch-level success or failure.

**Server-confirmed action**:
An action whose durable or external effect is not treated as complete until the server confirms it, including approvals, ledger pushes, and other financial writes. Local optimistic feedback may precede confirmation only for reversible, low-risk changes.

**Touchless**:
A document whose extracted fields all met the workspace's confidence threshold and was pushed to the ledger without a human review step. Shown on a record as a fact once it has happened, not as a prediction or a pending state.
_Avoid_: Auto-approved, zero-touch

**Processing state**:
Where a queue row stands in the intake → review → approval path, shown as one mark at the row's leading edge. Exactly one of, in precedence order: Cancelled, Needs attention (a check blocked it, an escalation is open, or an approval was rejected), In review, Touchless, Approved. Ledger facts such as Synced or Paid are not processing states and are shown separately. Due-date urgency is not a processing state either.
_Avoid_: Status (the column of pills is broader), aging (that is the due-date signal)

**Confidence threshold**:
The single workspace-set score an extracted field must reach to count as confident. It is the same floor Touchless is judged against, so a field that clears it in a queue row would also clear it for Touchless. A field entered by a person, or never scored by extraction, has no confidence and shows no confidence claim at all — absence means "not an AI claim", not "low".
_Avoid_: High confidence, low confidence (as if they were fixed numbers), the internal stage cutoff or amount-band floors (those are gates, not the user-facing threshold)

## Public marketing and coverage

**Supported coverage**:
A jurisdiction with a registered, working jurisdiction pack that can support the relevant document-to-ledger workflow.
_Avoid_: Global support, available everywhere

**Roadmap coverage**:
A jurisdiction the product may support later but cannot currently accept for the relevant workflow. It must not be presented as available or used to qualify a current signup promise.
_Avoid_: Supported, coming soon (unless the rollout is an explicit product commitment)

**Trial**:
A time-bounded product-access period with an explicit start, expiry, and billing or cancellation path. DocuBite must not use this term publicly until those supporting paths exist.
_Avoid_: Free workspace, evaluation

**Account creation**:
The current public entry action: creating a DocuBite account before setting up or joining a workspace. It is not a trial start or a payment event.
_Avoid_: Start free trial, Subscribe

**Workspace storage cap**:
The hard limit of 200 MB of stored documents per workspace. It must be disclosed before an upload is accepted, even when it is omitted from the marketing CTA.
_Avoid_: Unlimited storage

**Connected accounting system**:
An external accounting platform a workspace can connect to today, currently QuickBooks Online or Xero.
_Avoid_: Available integration when the connector is not live

**Built-in ledger**:
DocuBite's own double-entry ledger destination. It is a product capability, not an external integration.
_Avoid_: Third-party integration

**Planned integration**:
A named future accounting destination shown as roadmap intent, not as a capability available today. Planned integrations must not be presented with vendor marks without approved permission.
_Avoid_: Supported, connected, coming soon

**Product capability**:
A public-facing product area organized around one coherent mechanism and the visitor outcome it enables. The current capability vocabulary is Document extraction, Controls & fraud, Close the books, Data health, and Integrations & API.
_Avoid_: Feature list, module

**Product overview**:
The public entry point that orients visitors to the product capability set before directing them to detailed capability pages.
_Avoid_: Feature dump, single-scroll feature wall

**Trust & security**:
The procurement-facing explanation of DocuBite's safeguards, data handling, access controls, auditability, and compliance posture. It is a trust destination, not a Product capability.
_Avoid_: Security feature, compliance promise

**Solution**:
A role-oriented explanation of how DocuBite fits a team's workflow. Document types describe capabilities and belong with Product, not with the role-oriented Solutions structure.
_Avoid_: Document type, industry page

**Document extraction**:
The Product capability that turns supported PDFs and images into reviewable structured rows with visible confidence and source provenance. It describes the extraction and review mechanism, not a guarantee that every input is readable.
_Avoid_: Perfect OCR, quality rescue

**Controls & fraud**:
The Product capability that applies explainable checks, gates, approval rules, and human review before risky workflow steps.
_Avoid_: Fraud prevention guarantee, autonomous approval

**Close the books**:
The Product capability that coordinates close checklists, gated period transitions, accrual drafts, aging, matching, and related month-end work.
_Avoid_: Automatic close, payment execution

**Data health**:
The Product capability that surfaces scored pipeline, ledger, and tax hygiene so teams can find drift before it becomes a reconciliation problem.
_Avoid_: Data correctness guarantee, audit certification

**Integrations & API**:
The Product capability for sending reviewed data to the built-in ledger, connected accounting systems, and workspace-scoped external systems through documented API and webhook surfaces.
_Avoid_: Universal integration, available connector when it is only planned

**Capability page**:
A detailed public Product page organized around one outcome, one mechanism, evidence-backed proof points, explicit limits, and one account-creation action.
_Avoid_: Feature dump, unsupported promise

## Resolution (autopilot, 2026-09-15)

Grilled in three rounds (model → IA → rendering) with `intent`, `impeccable critique`/`shape`, `grilling` and `domain-modeling`; every question answered with its ➡️ recommendation under the owner's standing delegation. Incumbent critique of Settings + Controls: **23/40** (`.impeccable/critique/2026-09-15T23-27-40Z__app-app-workspaces-workspaceid-chrome-settings.md`); in-page detector 1440/390: settings/workspace 10/9 · modules 11/8 · rules 7/5 · Controls 6/5 · Controls settings 10/5 · Approval workflows 11/9 (five of each are shell-level). No Admin screenshots exist in `docs/vic-ai-tour-2026-09-15/` (the ticket's `vic-admin-04.png` was never captured); §1–2 of the tour findings are the Admin record.

### The model (ADR 0002)

1. **Workspace is the Company.** Organization is additive above it (`Workspace.organizationId` nullable, `OrganizationMember { admin | member }`). Option B (re-keying 71 models) rejected. `docs/adr/0002-organization-above-workspace-workspace-is-the-company.md`.
2. **Organization membership never implies entity access.** `WorkspaceMember` stays the only grant; org-wide queries are `unscoped()` + `workspaceId IN (WorkspaceMember ids)`, never derived from `OrganizationMember`. RLS stays per-workspace.
3. **Two role axes, both minimal:** org `admin | member`; entity `owner | reviewer | member` unchanged. No Accountant/Approver import — Approver is a stage-assignment fact (glossary).
4. **Personal workspaces** stay, ungrouped, shown as "Personal"; never in Companies.
5. **Closing the 32-model scope-guard gap is a prerequisite** for the first cross-company screen → task ticket.
6. **Invitations** can name N companies with a role per company; acceptance writes N `WorkspaceMember` rows + one `OrganizationMember(member)`.
7. **Platform `User.role = "admin"`** stays a third, unrelated axis.
8. **Words:** "Company" in Admin and the switcher, "Workspace" for storage and URLs. Glossary gains Company, Organization, Admin, Configuration.

### The IA

9. **One rail item, "Admin", at the bottom of the rail; Controls leaves the primary spine** and its pages move into Admin (nothing removed). Rail: Invoices · POs │ Receipts · Bank Statements │ Exceptions · Payments (#251) · Finance · Archive; secondary Close · Health Checks; bottom Activity · Admin.
10. **Vic's two groups**, mapped:
    - ORGANIZATION: **Dashboard** (≥2 companies only) · **Companies** · **Users**
    - ‹COMPANY NAME›: **Configuration** (field table · autonomy, blocks, policy, bands · warn checks · AI extraction · email intake · Tax · "What's on" = Modules) · **Approval Flows** · **PO Mismatch Flows** · **Suppliers** (`settings/rules` + Controls › Vendors merged) · **Integrations** (+ Account mapping; absent when integrations are off)
    - Account-level items leave Admin: Security and Reset tour move to the account menu. Suppliers and Integrations are documented DocuBite additions to Vic's COMPANY group.
11. **Field table drives both the Detail pane and the queues, with a boundary:** per type, canonical keys (`lib/doc-types.ts`) + that type's `DocumentTemplate` custom fields, with Editable · Required · Width, ✕ on custom rows only. Editable/Required → Detail pane (Required feeds "Block approval if a required field is missing"); Width/order → each queue's **system views' default columns**; a user's saved view still overrides. Configuration chooses among #225's `QueueColumn`s, it does not invent columns. (Graduates the "Metadata-driven columns" fog.)
12. **Approval Flows** = today's list + editor plus a **Default flow** selector, off by default, with the consequence sentence "Starts on its own when an invoice reaches In review with no blocking check. Until one is chosen, approvals start by hand from the Invoices bulk bar." (#227 hand-off.)
13. **PO Mismatch Flows** = **Tolerances** (PO quantity %, match-variance %, each with its consequence and #228's "= only while View PO is on") + **Who approves a mismatch** (named approvers; in-force default "the current stage's approver", #227 decision 4). Controls › Matches' history becomes its read-only log.
14. **Users**: org-level list on the #225 Queue-screen shell; pane tabs Information · Companies (one section per company: entity role select, ✕ remove; "Add to a company"). Last-owner / last-reviewer guards carry over per company. Without an organization the same screen shows this company's members.
15. **Companies**: list (name · country · currency · tax · members · your role) on the same shell; pane = summary + **Open**. **Add a company** replaces the "Create a team workspace" card. Organization creation is explicit: first visit to Companies from a team workspace asks "Name your organization"; other team workspaces the same user owns get "Move into ‹org›". No auto-grouping.
16. **Dashboard**: Vic's three rollups only — open invoices · Ready to Approve · pending PO mismatch approvals per company, plain tables with links, no charts; shown only at ≥2 companies. Not reporting (#237's out-of-scope stands); it is the multi-company day. Named Dashboard as Vic; glossary says it is not the workspace home.
17. **Switcher** grouped by organization, role shown per entry, Personal last, filter input above 6 entries. **`/workspaces`** stays a forwarder with one membership and becomes the Companies picker with more. The collapsible icon rail stays (#224 Q5 exception).
18. **Phone**: Admin is desktop-only (#189). The 4th tab becomes **Account** (profile, security, switch company, sign out). Admin pages still render content-only when deep-linked, with a one-line "Admin is a desktop area" note. #232 gets a comment.
19. **State inventory** every execution ticket ships: no organization yet · one company (no Dashboard) · many companies · member-not-owner (read-only Configuration with "Ask an owner", replacing today's `notFound()`) · last owner / last reviewer · integrations off (section absent) · unsaved changes on navigate · save failed (field-adjacent, form preserved) · company removed while open.

### Rendering (Impeccable)

20. **Admin shell**: left nav with two captioned groups inside the Admin work area; rail collapses to the 56px icon rail on Admin as on queues. Evidence: the incumbent tab strip wraps to 2 lines at 1440 and 3 at 390.
21. **Primitives**: Controls' grammar wins — `Panel`, `Ledger`, `SettingToggle`, `font-display` 26px h1, hairline dividers, one `max-w` for all of Admin; `Card` retired from Admin; the `#e6ebf1`/`#f1f5f9`/`#dbe3ec` hairlines lifted into tokens first.
22. **Field table** 40px rows, doc-type switcher above (Invoice · Purchase Order · Receipt · Bank Statement), a real `<table>`. **Toggles**: `SettingToggle` block variant; the inline variant gains a visible explanation — no explanation may live only in `title`. Group headings are questions or consequences.
23. **Save**: explicit Save + Discard on a sticky bottom action bar, "Unsaved changes" marker and `beforeunload`; confirm-with-30-day-estimate kept for Touchless and extended to "Default approval flow" and "Remove last reviewer". Not autosave.
24. **Lists**: Users and Companies on the Queue-screen shell (62px rows, header band, Detail pane); Approval Flows and Suppliers stay Ledger-style lists with inline editors.
25. **Words**: rail "Admin"; groups "Organization · ‹Company name›"; "Jurisdiction" → **Tax**; the "firm/SMB mode" pill replaced by its consequence sentence where it matters; warn-check "Predicate" → **When**; the reference block rewritten as "Fields you can test", no source paths.
26. **Accessibility**: both nav landmarks named; `aria-current` on Admin nav; visible toggle explanations; list→pane keyboard flow from #225; pill contrast raised from 4.3:1 to ≥4.5:1.
27. **Measure**: "add a user to two companies with different roles" in one flow, ≤6 interactions; counter-metric: Touchless enabled-then-reverted within 24h must not rise; craft bar: Admin critique ≥28/40, zero page-specific in-page findings at 1440 and 390; settings destinations 15 → 8.

### Removals — pending owner sign-off (not decided by autopilot)

- **Settings › Templates** (`DocumentTemplate` extraction templates grouped by *file*; files/worksheets are unplugged by #238). Proposed: unplug; custom fields surface through Configuration's field table.
- **Settings › Reports** (dictation report templates; dictation is unplugged and the page already 404s). Proposed: unplug.
Until signed, both stay reachable as sections under Configuration. Sign-off ticket: see below.

### Action Summary (execution inherits this order)

Intent: `specify` (per-screen spec + copy matrix for Configuration, Users, Companies) → `journey` (invite-to-N-companies, organization creation, Move into org) → `fortify` (state inventory above) → `include` (landmarks, toggle explanations, table semantics) → `measure`.
Impeccable: `extract` (hairline tokens, Panel/Ledger as admin primitives) → `shape` per section → `layout` → `distill` (Configuration's groups ≤4 per screen) → `clarify` (Q25 words) → `adapt` (icon rail + phone Account slot) → `audit` → `polish`.

### Tickets

Execution: Admin shell + Configuration · Approval Flows + PO Mismatch Flows · Organization, Companies, Users, Dashboard. Task (AFK): close the scope-guard gap. Task (HITL): owner sign-off on the two unplugs. Wired below.

9. **One rail item, "Admin", at the bottom of the rail; Controls leaves the primary spine** and its pages move into Admin (nothing removed). Rail: Invoices · POs │ Receipts · Bank Statements │ Exceptions · Payments (#251) · Finance · Archive; secondary Close · Health Checks; bottom Activity · Admin.
10. **Vic's two groups**, mapped:
    - ORGANIZATION: **Dashboard** (≥2 companies only) · **Companies** · **Users**
    - ‹COMPANY NAME›: **Configuration** (field table · autonomy, blocks, policy, bands · warn checks · AI extraction · email intake · Tax · "What's on" = Modules) · **Approval Flows** · **PO Mismatch Flows** · **Suppliers** (`settings/rules` + Controls › Vendors merged) · **Integrations** (+ Account mapping; absent when integrations are off)
    - Account-level items leave Admin: Security and Reset tour move to the account menu. Suppliers and Integrations are documented DocuBite additions to Vic's COMPANY group.
11. **Field table drives both the Detail pane and the queues, with a boundary:** per type, canonical keys (`lib/doc-types.ts`) + that type's `DocumentTemplate` custom fields, with Editable · Required · Width, ✕ on custom rows only. Editable/Required → Detail pane (Required feeds "Block approval if a required field is missing"); Width/order → each queue's **system views' default columns**; a user's saved view still overrides. Configuration chooses among #225's `QueueColumn`s, it does not invent columns. (Graduates the "Metadata-driven columns" fog.)
12. **Approval Flows** = today's list + editor plus a **Default flow** selector, off by default, with the consequence sentence "Starts on its own when an invoice reaches In review with no blocking check. Until one is chosen, approvals start by hand from the Invoices bulk bar." (#227 hand-off.)
13. **PO Mismatch Flows** = **Tolerances** (PO quantity %, match-variance %, each with its consequence and #228's "= only while View PO is on") + **Who approves a mismatch** (named approvers; in-force default "the current stage's approver", #227 decision 4). Controls › Matches' history becomes its read-only log.
14. **Users**: org-level list on the #225 Queue-screen shell; pane tabs Information · Companies (one section per company: entity role select, ✕ remove; "Add to a company"). Last-owner / last-reviewer guards carry over per company. Without an organization the same screen shows this company's members.
15. **Companies**: list (name · country · currency · tax · members · your role) on the same shell; pane = summary + **Open**. **Add a company** replaces the "Create a team workspace" card. Organization creation is explicit: first visit to Companies from a team workspace asks "Name your organization"; other team workspaces the same user owns get "Move into ‹org›". No auto-grouping.
16. **Dashboard**: Vic's three rollups only — open invoices · Ready to Approve · pending PO mismatch approvals per company, plain tables with links, no charts; shown only at ≥2 companies. Not reporting (#237's out-of-scope stands); it is the multi-company day. Named Dashboard as Vic; glossary says it is not the workspace home.
17. **Switcher** grouped by organization, role shown per entry, Personal last, filter input above 6 entries. **`/workspaces`** stays a forwarder with one membership and becomes the Companies picker with more. The collapsible icon rail stays (#224 Q5 exception).

Group headings are questions or consequences.

24. **Lists**: Users and Companies on the Queue-screen shell (62px rows, header band, Detail pane); Approval Flows and Suppliers stay Ledger-style lists with inline editors.

Execution: Admin shell + Configuration · Approval Flows + PO Mismatch Flows · Organization, Companies, Users, Dashboard. Task (AFK): close the scope-guard gap. Task (HITL): owner sign-off on the two unplugs. Wired below.

# Autopilot report — #231 Shape the Admin area: Configuration, Approval Flows, Mismatch Flows, Users, Companies

- Map: #226 Make the operator app work like Vic.ai (grammar, not skin)
- Type: wayfinder:grilling · Started: 2026-09-15T23:20Z · Finished: 2026-09-15T23:45Z
- Outcome: resolved

## What I did

1. Claimed #231; loaded the map, the #230 research (`docs/research/multi-company-access.md` on `research/multi-company-access`), tour findings §1–2 and §6, CONTEXT.md, PRODUCT.md, #113/#189/#232, and the incumbent Settings and Controls sources.
2. Called `grilling`, `domain-modeling`, `intent` and `impeccable critique`. `impeccable context` did not run (the launcher path is not on the driver's allowlist — see Needs the owner); read PRODUCT.md directly. There is no DESIGN.md. Noted that the ticket's `vic-admin-04.png` does not exist in `docs/vic-ai-tour-2026-09-15/`; §1–2 of the tour findings are the Admin record.
3. Ran the critique: Assessment A as an isolated sub-agent (source-only — its Bash was denied, so no screenshots); Assessment B inline (⚠️ degraded banner) — static `impeccable detect` (2 findings) and the in-page detector on six surfaces at 1440/390 with screenshots. Synthesised to **23/40**, persisted `.impeccable/critique/2026-09-15T23-27-40Z__app-app-workspaces-workspaceid-chrome-settings.md` (first run for the slug).
4. Grilled in three rounds (model → IA → rendering), 27 questions, each answered with its ➡️ recommendation.
5. Wrote `docs/adr/0002-organization-above-workspace-workspace-is-the-company.md`; added Company, Organization, Admin, Configuration to `CONTEXT.md`.
6. Posted the resolution comment (https://github.com/petrose99/Wes-doc/issues/231#issuecomment-5689597834), closed #231, appended to the map's Decisions so far, graduated three fog items and retargeted three that pointed at #231.
7. Created #252–#256, attached them as sub-issues of #226, wired blocking (#253 ← #252; #254 ← #252, #255). Left #256 (owner sign-off) unblocked so it can be signed now. Commented the phone decision on #232.
8. Committed the ADR, glossary, critique snapshot and this report.

## Questions I answered on the owner's behalf

| # | Question | Answer taken | Why (rule/evidence) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Company = Workspace or Company below Workspace | Workspace is the Company; Organization additive above | #230 research: 71/80 models on `workspaceId`, ADR-001 one ledger per workspace, both isolation layers keyed on `workspace_id`; smallest reversible |
| 2 | Does org membership imply entity access | No | Ethical defaults / least privilege; Vic adds each entity explicitly (tour §Admin → Users) |
| 3 | One or two role axes | Two, minimal (org `admin|member`; entity roles unchanged) | Glossary already has Approver as a stage fact; #233 one-vocabulary rule |
| 4 | Personal workspace fate | Stays, ungrouped, "Personal", never in Companies | Retiring is a removal; smallest reversible |
| 5 | Cross-company queries | `unscoped()` + `workspaceId IN (WorkspaceMember ids)`; guard-set gap closed first (#255) | Research §Isolation |
| 6 | Invitations | One invite → N companies with a role each | Success criterion; Vic's Companies tab is the read side |
| 7 | Platform admin vs org admin | Unrelated axes | `lib/admin.ts`; research warning |
| 8 | Workspace vs Company as the word | Company in Admin/switcher; Workspace for storage/URLs | Vic wins ties; PRODUCT.md users say "client company" |
| 9 | Admin replaces Settings + Controls | Yes; one rail item Admin; Controls leaves the spine | Critique P1 (two trees, two "Settings", two "Rules"); map Notes said Controls' fate waits on #231 |
| 10 | Admin's two groups mapped onto 15 pages | Vic's ORGANIZATION / COMPANY; Suppliers + Integrations as DocuBite additions; Security + Reset tour to the account menu | Vic wins ties; account-level items are not company settings (critique Q3 on scope) |
| 11 | Field table drives columns or only the pane | Both, with a boundary (system-view defaults; saved views override; chooses among #225's columns) | Vic's Width column only makes sense on the list; #225 and the Saved view glossary entry |
| 12 | Approval Flows | Today's editor + Default flow, off by default | #227 hand-off; ethical default (no automation the owner didn't choose) |
| 13 | PO Mismatch Flows | Tolerances + Who approves a mismatch | #227 decision 4; #228 tolerances |
| 14 | Users | Org list on the Queue-screen shell, pane Information · Companies | Vic's Users list + right panel; #225 shell |
| 15 | Companies | List + pane + Add a company; explicit org creation, no auto-grouping | Autonomy principle; replaces the "Create a team workspace" card |
| 16 | Org Dashboard | Vic's three rollups, ≥2 companies only, no charts | Vic wins ties; #237's out-of-scope is reporting, this is triage |
| 17 | Switcher and `/workspaces` | Grouped by org, role shown, filter >6; picker with >1 membership | Research §"Either way the switcher needs"; #224 Q5 rail exception kept |
| 18 | Phone | Admin desktop-only; 4th tab becomes Account | #189 (mobile is Approval-only) |
| 19 | State inventory | Nine named states on every execution ticket | `fortify`; critique H6 (`notFound()` for members is a dead end) |
| 20 | Left nav vs tab strip | Left nav, two captioned groups, icon rail collapses | Screenshots: tabs wrap to 2 lines at 1440, 3 at 390; Vic |
| 21 | Card vs Panel grammar | Panel/Ledger/SettingToggle; Card retired; hairlines to tokens | Critique P1 #2; detector nested-cards ×3 only on the Card page |
| 22 | Field table + toggles | 40px rows, real `<table>`, visible explanations | Sam finding (explanation in `title` only); craft floor |
| 23 | Save model | Explicit Save + Discard on a sticky bar; confirm-with-estimate kept | Map's sticky-bar grammar; ethical default (no half-typed policy in force) |
| 24 | Lists | Users/Companies on queue shell; Flows/Suppliers as Ledger lists | Vic for the long lists; the stage editor needs the width |
| 25 | Words | Admin · Organization · ‹Company› · Tax · When; firm/SMB pill → consequence sentence | `clarify`/`articulate`; critique H2 |
| 26 | Accessibility | Named landmarks, `aria-current`, visible explanations, ≥4.5:1 pills | Detector low-contrast 4.3:1; `include` |
| 27 | Measure | Two-company invite ≤6 interactions; counter-metric on Touchless reverts; craft bar | `measure`; CLAUDE.md close bar |

Critique's own closing questions: priority = IA first; scope = all P1 + P2. (Brief: take the recommendation.)

## Decisions recorded

Workspace is the Company; Organization is an additive grouping that never grants access (ADR 0002). One rail item Admin; Controls folds in. Vic's two groups with Suppliers and Integrations added; account-level settings move to the account menu. Configuration's field table drives both the Detail pane and system-view columns. Default approval flow off by default; PO Mismatch Flows hold tolerances and the mismatch approver. Users and Companies on the Queue-screen shell; Dashboard only at ≥2 companies. Controls' Panel/Ledger grammar becomes the admin grammar; left nav, explicit Save on a sticky bar. Admin is desktop-only; the phone gets an Account tab. Full text: the resolution comment on #231.

## Tickets created / changed

- #252 task — Build the Admin area shell and Configuration (frontier; blocks #253, #254).
- #253 task — Build Approval Flows and PO Mismatch Flows (blocked by #252).
- #254 task — Build Organization, Companies, Users and the Admin Dashboard (blocked by #252, #255).
- #255 task (AFK) — Close the scope-guard gap (frontier).
- #256 task (HITL) — Owner sign-off: unplug Settings › Templates and › Reports (frontier, needs the owner).
- #232 — comment with the phone decision.
- Map #226 — Decisions so far appended; fog graduated: "Metadata-driven columns" → #252, "per-entity Admin Dashboard" and "the multi-workspace day" → #254; fog retargeted: payments approval flow → #253/#254, unit-price tolerance → #253, bank-reconciled ownership → #248.
- `CONTEXT.md` — Company, Organization, Admin, Configuration. `docs/adr/0002-…md` new.

## Scores and counts (rendered surfaces only)

Grilling ticket — no surface changed. Incumbent baseline for the execution tickets:

- Critique (Settings + Controls): **23/40**, 3 × P1, 2 × P2. Snapshot `.impeccable/critique/2026-09-15T23-27-40Z__app-app-workspaces-workspaceid-chrome-settings.md`.
- Static `impeccable detect`: 2 (`gray-on-color`, integrations mapping tables).
- In-page detector 1440 / 390: settings/workspace 10/9 · settings/modules 11/8 · settings/rules 7/5 · automation 6/5 · automation/settings 10/5 · automation/approvals 11/9. Five per page are shell-level (switcher gradient ×2, switcher text-overflow at 1440, Inter overuse, body height transition, body dark-glow).
- `evaluate`: not run — nothing rendered changed; the execution tickets carry the ≥80 bar.

## Needs the owner

- **#256 — sign the two unplugs** (Settings › Templates, Settings › Reports) or say no; #252 keeps both reachable under Configuration until then.
- **Driver allowlist:** `Bash(impeccable:*)` never matches the launcher at `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable`, and the sub-agents had no Bash at all. I ran the engine binary (`~/.impeccable/bin/0.1.5/impeccable`) through `node` (allowed) for `detect` and `critique-storage`, and copied the runner into `/tmp/scratch229` (it resolves `playwright` from its own path). Adding `Bash(.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable:*)` to `ALLOWED_TOOLS` would make future sessions honest instead of clever. `impeccable context` was skipped for the same reason.
- **Validate Priya:** the multi-company accountant is inferred from PRODUCT.md; no research backs the Users/Companies flows. Not blocking, but `investigate` before #254 would be cheap.
- Nothing was started that needs stopping: the dev server (:3000), live-server (:8400) and containers were already running before this session and were left as found.

As of 2026-09-15 the "no live in-browser detector pass" gap on map #177 is solved. Recipe:

- `.env` already has `DEV_AUTH_BYPASS=true` and `DATABASE_URL` pointing at the `docubite-devdb` container on `127.0.0.1:55433` (separate from the stale `docubite-db-1`, see [[docubite-local-db-access]]). A `next dev` server is usually already listening on :3000; dev workspace id `af91555d-7450-4b21-a8ac-73db092617c8`.
- Prisma CLI ignores `.env` here: `export $(grep '^DATABASE_URL=' .env | sed 's/"//g') && npx prisma migrate deploy`.
- Seed rows: `npx tsx --env-file .env scripts/seed-sample-docs.ts <workspaceId>` (4 invoices, 3 receipts; no file bytes, so the inline SplitPane stays on "Loading…").
- Playwright must match the cached browser build (`~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1243` ↔ `playwright@1.63`); `npm install playwright@latest` in the scratchpad. The runner is committed at `scripts/dev/detect-in-page.mjs`. No system browser: `npm install playwright` in the scratchpad + `npx playwright install chromium` works without root. Start `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable live-server --background` (prints port, usually 8400), then `page.addScriptTag({url:"http://localhost:8400/detect.js"})` and read console lines; kill the pid after.

**Why:** several sessions wrongly concluded a live pass was impossible; the static `impeccable detect` found 3 findings where the in-page overlay found 23–27.

**How to apply:** any rendered-surface ticket on this repo runs this before claiming done, and records the counts.

**After a host reboot (seen 2026-09-15):** `/tmp` is wiped, so the scratchpad Playwright install and the copied runner are gone — reinstall `playwright@1.63` in a fresh scratchpad dir. `docubite-devdb` does not auto-start: `docker start docubite-devdb`. The `next-server` pid you see in `ps` may be the docker web container's process, not a host dev server — check `ss -ltn | grep :3000`. Start the dev server from a script file, detached (`setsid nohup <script> &`); never `pkill -f "next dev"` — it matches the calling shell and kills the session's command (exit 144). The impeccable live-server also has to be restarted (`impeccable live-server --background`).

Shell redirects/404s inside the workspace segment stream in the RSC payload (the layout flushes first), so `curl` reports 200 for both — verify landing and not-found with Playwright, not status codes.

**`npm run dev` has a `predev` that deletes `.next` (seen 2026-09-15):** starting a second dev server while one is already on :3000 wipes the running server's build and it starts returning 500, while the new one lands on :3001. Check `ss -ltn | grep :3000` first; if a server is up, use it. If it is broken, kill both by pid and start one.

## Summary — #231 resolved

**Critique of the incumbent** (Settings + Controls): **23/40**, in-page detector 6–11 findings per page at 1440 (five of them shell-level). Assessment B ran degraded (sub-agents had no Bash); Assessment A ran isolated but source-only. Snapshot persisted.

**Decisions** (27 questions, three rounds, each answered with its ➡️ recommendation):
- **Workspace is the Company; Organization is additive above it and never grants entity access** — ADR 0002. Two minimal role axes; personal workspaces stay ungrouped; scope-guard gap closed before any cross-company screen.
- **One rail item "Admin"; Controls folds in.** Vic's two groups: Organization (Dashboard at ≥2 companies · Companies · Users) and ‹Company› (Configuration · Approval Flows · PO Mismatch Flows · Suppliers · Integrations). Security and Reset tour move to the account menu.
- Configuration's field table drives **both** the Detail pane and each queue's system-view default columns; Default approval flow off by default; PO Mismatch Flows hold tolerances + the mismatch approver.
- Rendering: Controls' Panel/Ledger grammar wins, left nav not a tab strip (the strip wraps at every width), explicit Save on a sticky bar, "Jurisdiction" → Tax. Admin is desktop-only; the phone gets an Account tab.

**Tracker:** #231 closed with the resolution comment; map Decisions appended, three fog items graduated, three retargeted. New tickets: **#252** shell + Configuration (frontier) → **#253** Flows, **#254** Organization/Users (also waits on **#255** scope-guard task, frontier). **#256** owner sign-off on unplugging Settings › Templates and › Reports — the one thing I did not decide. Glossary gained Company, Organization, Admin, Configuration. Commit `ba57479`; report at `docs/wayfinder-reports/226/231.md`.

**Needs the owner:** sign #256; and add `Bash(.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable:*)` to the driver's allowlist — the current `Bash(impeccable:*)` pattern never matches, so I ran the engine through `node` this session and recorded the workaround in memory.

result:
Session complete. Nothing to stop: the dev server, live-server and containers were running before I started and I left them as found.

## Summary — #231 resolved

**Critique of the incumbent** (Settings + Controls): **23/40**, in-page detector 6–11 findings per page at 1440 (five of them shell-level). Assessment B ran degraded (sub-agents had no Bash); Assessment A ran isolated but source-only. Snapshot persisted.

**Decisions** (27 questions, three rounds, each answered with its ➡️ recommendation):
- **Workspace is the Company; Organization is additive above it and never grants entity access** — ADR 0002. Two minimal role axes; personal workspaces stay ungrouped; scope-guard gap closed before any cross-company screen.
- **One rail item "Admin"; Controls folds in.** Vic's two groups: Organization (Dashboard at ≥2 companies · Companies · Users) and ‹Company› (Configuration · Approval Flows · PO Mismatch Flows · Suppliers · Integrations). Security and Reset tour move to the account menu.
- Configuration's field table drives **both** the Detail pane and each queue's system-view default columns; Default approval flow off by default; PO Mismatch Flows hold tolerances + the mismatch approver.
- Rendering: Controls' Panel/Ledger grammar wins, left nav not a tab strip (the strip wraps at every width), explicit Save on a sticky bar, "Jurisdiction" → Tax. Admin is desktop-only; the phone gets an Account tab.

**Tracker:** #231 closed with the resolution comment; map Decisions appended, three fog items graduated, three retargeted. New tickets: **#252** shell + Configuration (frontier) → **#253** Flows, **#254** Organization/Users (also waits on **#255** scope-guard task, frontier). **#256** owner sign-off on unplugging Settings › Templates and › Reports — the one thing I did not decide. Glossary gained Company, Organization, Admin, Configuration. Commit `ba57479`; report at `docs/wayfinder-reports/226/231.md`.

**Needs the owner:** sign #256; and add `Bash(.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable:*)` to the driver's allowlist — the current `Bash(impeccable:*)` pattern never matches, so I ran the engine through `node` this session and recorded the workaround in memory.
